shots.notes: The room and the host. The chapter's title belongs to the opener, not to a slot here.

The camera above the desk, looking down at what he is walking through. `room/surface` is the only role `high-desk-down` fills, and it is the one angle in the kit with no floor in shot — it declares `hostAnchor: false` and nobody stands in it. A filing walk is the beat that wants it: the document is the subject, not the man reading it.

What a filing-walk chapter is for, in a plate the kit allows it. Prose goes in prose slots: a label holds thirty characters and is for a metric name, not a sentence. He is beside it, in medium, looking at it. The graphic takes a column and he takes the other — the glance toward it is the pipeline's, off which side the graphic landed on, and a chapter where the evidence is the whole point keeps the frame to itself.
Back to him to land it. `to-camera` is the close-up and the medium — the framings carry the lines that matter.
